page.title: Passive Reporting Structures
page.subtitle_html: Passive Reporting Structures - C1 impersonal passive, personal passive, and perfect infinitive reporting patterns.
page.subtitle_text: C1 impersonal passive, personal passive, and perfect infinitive reporting patterns.

blocks.body: {"level":"C1","intro":"Passive Reporting Structures: compact C1 anchors for it is said that, he is said to, and perfect infinitive reporting structures.","rules":[{"label":"Impersonal passive","text":"Use it is said, believed, thought, reported, or claimed that + clause.","example":"It is believed that the plan will succeed."},{"label":"Personal passive","text":"Use subject + is or are said/believed/thought/reported + to + verb.","example":"The company is reported to employ 500 people."},{"label":"Perfect infinitive","text":"Use to have + past participle for a reported earlier action.","example":"He is said to have left the country."}]}

page.title: Complex Passive and Causative
page.subtitle_html: Complex Passive and Causative - C1 passive reporting, causative have/get, and formal passive patterns.
page.subtitle_text: C1 passive reporting, causative have/get, and formal passive patterns.

blocks.body: {"level":"C1","intro":"Complex Passive and Causative: compact anchors for advanced passive and causative patterns.","rules":[{"label":"Causative have/get","text":"Use have or get + object + past participle when someone arranges for an action to be done.","example":"I had my car repaired at the garage."},{"label":"Complex passive","text":"Use passive forms with reporting, infinitives, and formal processes when the action matters more than the agent.","example":"The policy is expected to be revised."},{"label":"Formal focus","text":"Passive and causative forms often create a neutral or institutional tone in C1 writing.","example":"The documents were reviewed before the decision was announced."}]}

page.title: Complex Passive Impersonal Style
page.subtitle_html: Complex Passive Impersonal Style - C2 impersonal passive and reporting-passive patterns.
page.subtitle_text: C2 impersonal passive and reporting-passive patterns.

blocks.body: {"level":"C2","intro":"Complex passive and impersonal style: compact anchors for formal reporting structures with it, personal passive subjects, and perfect infinitives.","rules":[{"label":"Impersonal passive","text":"Use It is believed that, It is reported that, and similar forms to present claims without naming the source.","example":"It is believed that this policy reduces risk."},{"label":"Personal passive","text":"Move the reported subject forward with is said to, is thought to, or is expected to.","example":"The policy is believed to reduce risk."},{"label":"Perfect passive reporting","text":"Use passive perfect infinitives when the reported action happened earlier.","example":"The errors are reported to have been found."}]}

blocks.heading: C2 focus
blocks.body: This compact page anchors the English Sentence Builder C2 lesson on complex passive and impersonal style.
